questions.question_text: A revolving water cannon sprays a sector of ground of radius $6$ m as it turns through $210^{\circ}$. Find the area sprayed, correct to the nearest square metre.

options.why: Found the area of the whole circle and ignored that only part of it is sprayed.
Used $2\pi r$ instead of $\pi r^{2}$, giving the arc length rather than an area.
Divided the angle by $180$ instead of $360$, doubling the fraction of the circle.
Gave the area of the whole cake instead of one twelfth of it.
Substituted the diameter $28$ cm in place of the radius before taking a twelfth.
Took a twelfth of the circumference $2\pi r$ instead of a twelfth of the area.

questions.solution_text:
One slice is $\frac{1}{12}$ of the circle.
$A = \frac{1}{12} \times \pi r^{2}$
$= \frac{1}{12} \times \pi(14)^{2}$
$= \frac{196}{12}\pi$
$= \frac{49}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A sector has a radius of $10$ cm, and its interior angle is three times its exterior angle. Find the exact area of the sector, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used the exterior angle of $90^{\circ}$ in the formula instead of the interior angle.
Gave the area of the whole circle without applying the fraction at all.
Reversed the ratio, taking the interior angle as one third of the full turn.

questions.solution_text:
The two angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, and the interior is three times the exterior, so the full turn splits into $4$ equal parts.
$\text{exterior} = 360^{\circ} \div 4 = 90^{\circ}$
$\theta = 3 \times 90^{\circ} = 270^{\circ}$
$A = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}$
$= \frac{270}{360} \times \pi(10)^{2}$
$= \frac{3}{4} \times 100\pi$
$= 75\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
